newsitem.title: USA: Group patenting biotech polymer intermediate.
newsitem.headline: Group patenting biotech polymer intermediate.

text.p: DuPont Co and Genencor International Inc have filed worldwide patents for processes and microorganisms that produce 1,3-propanediol -- used in producing a form of polyester -- in a single step from virtually any carbohydrate source, DuPont said Monday.
The two agreed to develop a biological process for 1,3-propanediol, known as 3G.
Genencor is a joint venture of Eastman Chemical Co and Cultor Oy.
3G, a large volume polymer intermediate, is an ingredient in the production of 3GT, a form of polyester with properties that exceed many of those of the traditional form of polyester, known as PET.
DuPont said the biotechnology will facilitate production of 3G at a cost approaching that of ethylene glycol, the monomer used to produce PET.
It also said 3GT polyester can be produced in existing Dacron polyester fiber production facilities with only minor modifications, and in planned new nylon fiber production facilities.
In mid-November, DuPont said it would invest $150 million a year over the next five years to modernize its nylon facilities.
